title: Trademark Prosecution in Practice
subtitle: Ten recorded sessions that take one mark from the first search to the hearing notice: search reports, risk calls, examination report responses and written submissions, drafted the way the Registry expects them.
summary: The complete prosecution cycle in fifteen two-hour sessions, all recorded. Half the course is the pre-filing search most juniors are never taught properly; the other half is the examination report, the written submission and the hearing, including five live demonstrations on real Registry examination reports and written submissions covering every type of objection. Fifteen practice exercises, email support throughout, and a community of IP professionals.
outcomes: Classify a proposed mark and predict its Section 9 and Section 11 exposure before anyone files
Build search strings that find phonetic, visual and transliterated variants the plain search misses
Prepare a complete pre-filing search report with a risk opinion a client can act on
Run dilution, proprietor and WIPO Global Brand Database searches, and know when transborder reputation matters
Read a Registry examination report in minutes and choose the right route for each objection
Draft a response to a Section 9 or Section 11 objection with the evidence index to back it
Prepare written submissions and a hearing file that survive the hearing officer's questions
Keep a prosecution docket clean: deadlines, file hygiene and the records the Registry will ask for
Answer every type of Registry objection, formal, Section 9 and Section 11, and the hearing notice that follows, from real worked examples
about: Most trademark training starts at the examination report. This course starts earlier, where the real decisions are made: the search. Six of the fifteen sessions are about finding what is already on the Register and on the market, reading it under Sections 9, 11 and 17, and writing an opinion that tells the client whether to file, change the mark, or walk away.

The second half is prosecution proper. You read real Registry examination reports, choose the route for each objection, draft the response, and then prepare the written submission and hearing file for the matters that are not waived. Five sessions are pure demonstration: real examination reports and hearing notices of every type, from a Section 9(1)(a) objection to a combined report and a post-hearing written submission, answered live on screen from the first line to the annexure list.

Every session is recorded, and the recordings stay open to you for two months from the date you register: long enough to work through all fifteen at two sessions a week with time to spare, and to return to the parts you need on a live matter. Fifteen practice exercises, one per session, come with model answers. Questions go by email and are answered by the people who teach the course. Enrolling also places you in the VIDIKSHA community of IP professionals, where practitioners compare notes on real objections and Registry practice.

You also receive the IP Prosecution Kit at your doorstep: the Vidiksha Trademark Prosecution in Practice book, the prosecution and filing checklists, and the sample drafts the course is built around, printed, so they are on your desk when a real examination report lands.

modules.title: Basics of trademark law in India
lessons: What a trademark protects, and what it does not
Kinds of marks: word, device, composite, shape, colour, sound, collective and certification marks
Section 9: the absolute grounds, limb by limb
Section 11: the relative grounds and the earlier mark
Section 17: composite marks, disclaimers and the exclusive right to the whole
Practice exercise 1: classify eight proposed marks and flag the section each will meet

modules.title: Pre-filing search I: the report and the Section 9 analysis
lessons: Anatomy of a trademark search report and what the client actually reads
Section 9 analysis of the proposed mark: descriptive, laudatory, customary, non-distinctive
Search strings: truncation, phonetic equivalents, transliteration and spelling variants
Reading similar marks on the Register: status, class, specification and proprietor
Prosecution hygiene: file naming, docket entries, deadlines and the records to keep from day one
Practice exercise 2: write the search strings and Section 9 note for a given mark

modules.title: Pre-filing search II: Section 11, common law and the internet
lessons: Section 11 analysis against cited marks: visual, phonetic and conceptual comparison
Goods, trade channels and the 'same description' question
Common-law rights: unregistered marks, prior use and passing off exposure
Internet search for high-risk citations: marketplaces, domains, social media, company names
Weighing the citations: which ones block, which ones can be designed around
Practice exercise 3: Section 11 and common-law analysis for three cited marks

modules.title: Pre-filing search demonstration: the full report
lessons: A real brief, worked live from first search to signed opinion
Structuring the report: findings, risk table, recommendation, next steps
Phrasing a risk opinion a client can act on without a second call
Practice exercise 4: prepare a complete search report on a mark of your choice

modules.title: Dilution search and proprietor search
lessons: Well-known marks and dilution under Section 11(2): when dissimilar goods still block
Running a dilution search and reading the well-known marks list
Proprietor search: mapping an opponent's or client's whole portfolio
Spotting house marks, families of marks and abandoned applications
Practice exercise 5: dilution and proprietor search for a consumer brand

modules.title: WIPO Global Brand Database and transborder reputation
lessons: Searching the WIPO Global Brand Database: Madrid designations, national collections, image search
Marks designating India under the Madrid Protocol and what they mean for your search
Transborder reputation: the doctrine, the evidence courts have accepted, and how to search for it
Writing the international section of a search report
Practice exercise 6: international search and transborder reputation note

modules.title: Examination reports and responses
lessons: Anatomy of a Registry examination report and where the real objection hides
Formal objections, cleared in a sentence
Section 9 objections: inherent distinctiveness or acquired distinctiveness, and the evidence each needs
Section 11 objections: comparing marks and goods the way the Registry does, consents and limitations
Structure of the response and the one-month deadline
Practice exercise 7: draft a full response to a combined Section 9 and Section 11 report

modules.title: Written submissions and hearing notices
lessons: From hearing notice to hearing day: timeline and paperwork
Written submissions: what to concede, what to argue, what to annex
Preparing the hearing file and the two-minute opening
What hearing officers ask, and what they decide on
Adjournments, review and what happens after refusal
Practice exercise 8: written submissions for a Section 11 hearing

modules.title: Demonstration: examination report response and written submissions
lessons: A real examination report answered live, paragraph by paragraph
Building the evidence index and the affidavit of use on screen
The written submission for the same matter, drafted live
Practice exercise 9: respond to a new examination report using the demonstrated method

modules.title: Full walk-through: from pre-filing to hearing notice
lessons: One mark, end to end: search, opinion, filing, examination report, response, hearing
Where files go wrong, and the checkpoints that catch it
Your prosecution toolkit: the templates, checklists and docket you leave with
Practice exercise 10: run the full cycle on a mark and submit the file for review

modules.title: Live demonstration I: Section 9(1)(a) objection, acquired distinctiveness
lessons: A real examination report objecting that the mark is devoid of distinctive character, read line by line
Deciding the route: why inherent distinctiveness will not carry this mark and acquired distinctiveness will
Building the evidence index on screen: date of first use, invoices across years, advertising spend, sales figures, market presence
Drafting the user affidavit and the response, paragraph by paragraph, with the annexures numbered as the Registry expects
Practice exercise 11: respond to a Section 9(1)(a) report with the evidence pack provided

modules.title: Live demonstration II: Section 9(1)(b) and 9(1)(c), descriptive, laudatory and customary marks
lessons: Three real reports: a descriptive word, a laudatory word and a term that has become customary in the trade
Suggestive or descriptive: the argument that keeps a mark on the inherent-distinctiveness route, and the decisions that support it
When to disclaim, when to amend the mark, when to limit the specification, and when to concede and refile
Drafting the three responses live, with the precedents cited the way hearing officers prefer
Practice exercise 12: classify five marks on the 9(1)(b) spectrum and draft the response for the hardest one

modules.title: Live demonstration III: Section 11 citations, distinguishing, consent and rectification
lessons: A real report citing two earlier marks: comparing marks and goods the way the Registry does, visually, phonetically and conceptually
Checking the cited marks first: status, renewal, proprietor, evidence of use, and whether a Section 47 rectification is the better reply
Consents, coexistence and limitation of specification: drafting the letter of consent and the limited specification
Drafting the Section 11 response live, including the comparison table the Registry reads first
Practice exercise 13: answer a Section 11 citation two ways, by distinguishing and by limitation, and choose one

modules.title: Live demonstration IV: the combined report, formal, Section 9 and Section 11 objections together
lessons: A real report with every type of objection at once: classification, specification, proprietor details, user claim, Section 9 and Section 11
Clearing the formal objections in a sentence each, and the TM-M amendments that go with them
Ordering the response so the Registry reads the strongest point first
Drafting the complete response live, start to finish, with the full evidence index and annexure list
Practice exercise 14: respond to a combined report under the one-month deadline

modules.title: Live demonstration V: written submissions after the hearing notice, every type of hearing
lessons: Three real hearing notices: a Section 9 hearing, a Section 11 hearing and a hearing after a deficient response
What to concede, what to argue and what to annex in a written submission, and the fifteen-day timeline
Drafting the written submissions live, with the evidence of use, the precedents and the two-minute opening for the hearing day
After the hearing: review, appeal to the High Court and refiling, and how to advise the client on each
Practice exercise 15: prepare the written submission package for a Section 11 hearing notice

kit.title: IP Prosecution Kit

In-house counsel who review outside counsel's search reports and prosecution work
Founders who want to clear and file their own marks with open eyes
Final-year law students who want a job that involves this

You have never opened the Trade Marks Act and want to start there
You do only litigation and never touch the Registry

faq.a: Recorded. All fifteen sessions are available from the day you enrol, so you can watch at your own pace and go back to a session when a live matter needs it. Questions go by email and are answered by the instructors.
faq.q: Are the sessions live or recorded?

faq.a: Two months from the date of registration. That is comfortably enough for the fifteen sessions and the exercises; if you need longer for a good reason, write to us before the period ends.
faq.q: How long do I have access to the recordings?

faq.a: The Vidiksha Trademark Prosecution in Practice book, the prosecution checklist, the checklist for filing a trademark, and printed sample drafts for examination report responses, written submissions, and Section 9, Section 11 and common-law clearances. It is couriered to the address you give at registration, within India.
faq.q: What is in the IP Prosecution Kit, and how does it reach me?

faq.a: A private group of VIDIKSHA members who practise IP: associates, in-house counsel, agents and founders. It is where people compare notes on real objections, hearing experiences and Registry practice, and where we post updates when practice changes.
Indian practice under the Trade Marks Act, 1999 and the Trade Marks Rules, 2017, as applied by the Registry today. Sessions are re-recorded when practice changes.
faq.q: Which Registry practice does this follow?

faq.a: Yes. Search reports, examination reports, responses, written submissions and hearing records from actual matters, with client and mark details altered where needed.
